gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how many days each rugged watch lasts on a trip with 6 hours of full-accuracy GPS a day and smartwatch use the rest of the day. On Garmin's, Amazfit's and Apple's own ratings that comes to about 7.1 days for the fēnix 8 Pro 51 mm, 5.9 for the Amazfit T-Rex 3, 5.3 for the T-Rex 3 Pro, 5.1 for the Instinct 3 Solar 50 mm, 3.6 for the Instinct 3 Solar 45 mm (6.7 with sun) and 1.4 for the Apple Watch Ultra 4.
standout_why: I compared against mobileplustech.com, the cited guide. It gives no battery numbers at all and computes nothing; it says Garmin solar models 'state the longest battery estimates' and Apple is 'rated for days rather than weeks'. The cited TechRadar T-Rex 3 Pro review cut off after its headline when I fetched it, so it may state the 25-day or 38-hour rating, but I could not check whether it does any trip arithmetic. Neither page puts the watches on one per-trip scale, and neither shows that the $279.99 T-Rex 3 outlasts the Instinct 3 Solar 45 mm when there's no sun.
decides: It confirms that Apple should not be the pick for a multi-day outdoor trip: at 6 hours of GPS a day the Ultra 4 needs a charge every 1.4 days, while every Garmin and Amazfit candidate goes 3.6 to 7.1 days. It also changes the value pick. ChatGPT made the Instinct 3 Solar its overall pick but showed the 45 mm price. That size only beats the $279.99 T-Rex 3 (6.7 days vs 5.9) if Garmin's 50,000-lux solar assumption holds. In normal sun-poor conditions the T-Rex 3 lasts longer (5.9 vs 3.6 days), so the Instinct only clearly wins in its 50 mm size or for people who spend all day in strong sun.

findings.label: Duty cycle and formula used for every figure
findings.value: 6 h GPS + 18 h smartwatch per day
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual – Battery Life Information
findings.note: Days per charge = 1 / (6/GPS_h + 18/(smartwatch_days×24)). GPS mode used: Garmin 'All satellite systems plus multi-band', Amazfit 'Accurate GPS', Apple outdoor workout. These are each maker's highest-accuracy mode, so they are roughly comparable. All inputs are maker ratings, not lab measurements.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h multi-band GPS/day, no solar
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual – Battery Life Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch 28 days, all-systems + multi-band 24 h. Math: 1/(6/24 + 18/672) = 1/(0.250+0.027) = 3.6 days. In all-systems mode without multi-band (28 h) it is 1/(0.214+0.027) = 4.1 days.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h multi-band GPS/day, with Garmin's solar assumption
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual – Battery Life Information
findings.note: Inputs: multi-band 40 h with solar, smartwatch 'unlimited with solar' (Garmin assumes 3 h/day outdoors at 50,000 lux; the GPS figure assumes outdoor use at 50,000 lux). Math: 1/(6/40 + 0) = 6.7 days. This only holds in bright sun.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h multi-band GPS/day, no solar
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual – Battery Life Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch 40 days, multi-band 34 h. Math: 1/(6/34 + 18/960) = 1/(0.176+0.019) = 5.1 days. With solar (60 h, unlimited smartwatch): 1/(6/60) = 10 days.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h multi-band GPS/day (gesture display)
findings.source_title: fēnix 8 Series Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch 27 days (gesture), all-systems + multi-band (SatIQ) 53 h. Math: 1/(6/53 + 18/648) = 1/(0.113+0.028) = 7.1 days. With the always-on display (15 days, 41 h): 1/(0.146+0.050) = 5.1 days.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h multi-band GPS/day (gesture display)
findings.source_title: fēnix 8 Series Owner's Manual – Battery Information
findings.note: Inputs: smartwatch 15 days, multi-band 30 h. Math: 1/(6/30 + 18/360) = 1/(0.200+0.050) = 4.0 days.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h Accurate GPS/day
findings.note: Inputs: typical use 27 days, Accurate GNSS 42 h (700 mAh, 68.3 g without strap). Math: 1/(6/42 + 18/648) = 1/(0.143+0.028) = 5.9 days. Amazfit's own US and UK pages returned HTTP 429 every time, so these maker ratings come from a named spec reviewer.

findings.label: Price, Amazfit US store
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of us.amazfit.com; no compare-at price, in stock. The listing says 'Over 3 weeks of battery life during typical use'.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h Accurate GPS/day
findings.note: Inputs: typical use 25 days, Accurate GPS 38 h (700 mAh, 52 g without strap). Math: 1/(6/38 + 18/600) = 1/(0.158+0.030) = 5.3 days. The US store listing confirms 'Up to 25 days battery life (48mm)'.

findings.label: Price, Amazfit US store
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of us.amazfit.com; no compare-at price, in stock.

findings.label: Days per charge, 6 h outdoor workout/day
findings.note: Inputs: up to 50 h normal use, up to 18 h workout tracking (outdoor run, heart rate on, no iPhone). Math: 1/(6/18 + 18/50) = 1/(0.333+0.360) = 1.4 days. Apple's 50 h test already includes two 60-min workouts, so this slightly double-counts. With Max Extended Workout (45 h, Low Power Mode, alerts off): 1/(6/45 + 18/50) = 2.0 days.
